notes: One section type renders both replaced originals: the product opener (5-star review badge, teen-vitamin H1, subheading, anchor CTA, guarantee line, animated sales badge with 3 images, Alyssa testimonial card) and the founder closer (deficiency headline, three stat cards, Try Now CTA). Easy to miss: the original duplicated desktop+mobile DOM, so the rebuild's single responsive DOM must show exactly 2 CTAs page-wide (not 4), both pure anchors to #standalone-product-section which must exist for clicks to do anything; and the founder stats are sentences with a strict reading order — 'Are Found In' precedes '59%' — that a value-first card layout silently garbles. No videos and no path links in this section, so video-playing and no-broken-links are intentionally omitted in favor of the anchor-target check.

assertions.why: Both original heroes' CTAs link to #standalone-product-section (extraction a-open nodes); exactly one CTA per hero instance in the responsive DOM — 0/1 means a hero is missing, >2 means duplicated instances or leftover desktop+mobile DOM.
Behaviour: clicking either hero CTA must scroll to the buy box. no-broken-links never checks # anchors, so without this the CTAs could be silent no-ops that look perfect in a screenshot.
The original review badge draws 5 star icons; a screenshot won't count them. Scoping to --product also proves the opener instance uses the product style (the founder hero has no badge).
Trust-badge copy byte-for-byte from the extraction (seq 44), including the comma-formatted count and the plus sign.

assertions.why: The opener headline must be an H1 (only the product hero uses H1) and carry the three extraction fragments (seq 47-49) joined in original order, including the highlighted middle span's text.

assertions.why: Full subheading sentence assembled from extraction seq 54-56 in order, including the literal ampersand and the exact nutrient/superfood counts.
CTA label byte-for-byte from the extraction (seq 63) — the two emoji are the first thing a retyped label or encoding bug drops.

assertions.why: Guarantee line under the product CTA (seq 79) including the trailing double asterisk that ties to the page's fine print.
Social-proof sales badge copy assembled byte-for-byte from extraction seq 90-91 (bold count + plain suffix read as one phrase).
The original badge carries an animated GIF plus two overlapping gummy icons (3 img nodes in the extraction) — small decorations a compressed screenshot hides and a sizing bug can blow up full-width.

assertions.contains: My son is VERY picky but gets so excited to eat these. I unfortunately tried hiya first & wasted money because he would not eat them. I love that these are a gummy soft chewable. Alyssa Blossom
assertions.why: Full testimonial quote byte-for-byte from the extraction (seq 108) immediately followed by the author name (seq 114) inside the same card — proves quote, attribution, and their order in one check.

assertions.contains: 1 in 3 Families Have A Nutrient Deficiency.
assertions.why: Founder-closer headline byte-for-byte from the second original (seq 45) — proves the second instance carries its own content, not a copy of the first.
The original founder hero lists exactly 3 statistics (microplastics / additives / lost nutrients); the scoped selector also proves the closer instance uses the founder style.

assertions.contains: The Average Person Consumes 52 Credit Cards’ Worth Of Microplastics Every Year.
assertions.why: First stat sentence assembled from extraction seq 52-56 in order — the curly apostrophe in Cards’ (U+2019) is byte-for-byte and exactly what retyping silently loses.

assertions.contains: Artificial Food Additives Are Found In 59% Of Foods Today
assertions.why: The original bullet reads plain/highlight interleaved in THIS order (seq 59-62): 'Are Found In' before '59%'. A card layout that always renders the highlighted value second garbles the sentence — the sequence must be contiguous in the rendered text.
The hero image, pill CTA with emoji, sales badge, and 3-card stat row are the likely 390px overflow culprits; the original keeps both hero instances inside the viewport.
